extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, and newsrooms interested in producing or evaluating solutions journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and evaluating solutions journalism: stories that report on responses to social problems, assess evidence and limitations, and distill lessons or insights useful to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: All four pillars present
rubrics_metrics.description: Each solutions story should contain all four pillars to some degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria inspire the network and are the foundation of how solutions journalism is defined in practice and for the Solutions Story Tracker®. They can be applied with flexibility for diverse narrative styles and story formats, but a solutions story should include all four pillars (response-focus, insight, evidence, limitations) to some degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on a response to a social problem
rubrics_metrics.description: A solutions story focuses on a RESPONSE to a social problem — and how that response has worked or why it hasn’t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the story doesn’t describe a response, it’s not solutions journalism. The response should be explained in the context of the problem it’s trying to address, and the story should delve into how it works. The narrative is driven by the problem-solving; tension resides in the inherent difficulty of solving the problem. Documenting the causes of the problem helps clarify the opportunity for a solution to create leverage and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distills lessons and offers insight
rubrics_metrics.description: The best solutions reporting distills the lessons that make the response relevant and accessible to others — in other words, it offers INSIGHT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What makes solutions journalism compelling is the discovery—the journey that brings the reader or viewer to an insight about how the world works and, perhaps, how it could be made to work better. Reporting should surface transferable lessons or takeaways that others can learn from.

rubrics_metrics.name: Looks for evidence of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions journalism looks for EVIDENCE — data or qualitative results that show effectiveness (or lack thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be upfront with audiences about what the evidence tells us and what it doesn’t. A particularly innovative response can still be newsworthy with little evidence, but the reporter must be transparent about the lack of evidence and explain why the response merits coverage despite that gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on limitations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions stories must reveal a response’s shortcomings. No response is perfect; some work well for one community but may fail in others. A responsible reporter covers what doesn’t work and places the response in context so readers understand boundaries, trade-offs, and generalizability.
